newsitem.title: INDIA: Tight U.S. soymeal supplies to help Indian prices.
newsitem.headline: Tight U.S. soymeal supplies to help Indian prices.

text.p: Tight U.S. soymeal supplies up to January could push up Indian export prices, traders said on Monday.
The United States and India are among main soymeal suppliers in the Far East markets.
"There are possibilities for Indian soymeal prices to pick up in domestic and international markets," S.N. Saboo, of broking firm S.S. Mercantile told Reuters.
Reports from Chicago quoted dealers saying at the weekend tight U.S. supplies this autumn have frustrated bargain hunters who have held off purchases hoping cash basis levels would fall.
Instead basis levels have risen, supported by a late U.S. soybean harvest and active soymeal export programme. As a result very little soymeal is available for November or December needs.
Traders said Indian soymeal prices on Monday were steady but the undertone was weak.
Indian soymeal was quoted at $262-263 per tonne FAS on Friday at Indore, the hub of India's soybean industry.

Traders expected the prices to move up to $270 per tonne in a week's time. They forecast soymeal availability in the 1996/97 (November-October) season to be lower than anticipated due to a fall in soybean output.
Traders estimated the 1996/97 soybean crop at 3.9 million tonnes compared to 4.2 million in the previous season.
Farmers retain a portion of the crop for seed purposes for the next season.
Traders said the fall in output would leave only 3.4 million tonnes of soybean for crushing compared to about 4.0 million tonnes in 1995/96.

The Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA) on Friday pegged the 1996/97 soybean crop at 4.0 million tonnes. It had earlier seen output at 4.4 million tonnes but lowered it after excessive rains in the last week of October.
